ASUS Vivobook 15, 15.6" Thin and Light Laptop, FHD (1920x1080) Display, Intel Core 5 320, 16GB, 512GB

reviews.quote: The Vivobook 15 cuts a few corners to keep its cost down and the display is dull, but its performance is right up there with laptops that cost a couple thousand bucks more.
An inexpensive laptop that performs well — good performance and comfort under heavy loads, comfortable keyboard, and cooling that quietly does its job.

praises: 16GB DDR5 in an upgradable SO-DIMM slot — rare at this price and future-proof
Core 5 320 handles office work, dozens of tabs, and video calls without stutter
Webcam has a physical privacy shutter, which most budget rivals omit
Numeric keypad fits a 1.7 kg 15.6" chassis — appreciated for spreadsheet work
At the $849.99 sale it undercuts nearly every 16GB FHD competitor
complaints: 250-nit panel is genuinely dim indoors and useless outdoors; colours look washed out
USB-C is data-only — no power delivery or DisplayPort, and charging is a DC barrel only
Lid and keyboard deck flex noticeably; middle hinge wobbles when typing
BestBuy spec sheet falsely flags it as a Copilot+ PC — the Core 5 320 has no NPU

standouts: Upgradable 16GB DDR5 SO-DIMM plus 16GB-from-box: the safest long-term RAM story in the budget class
design_philosophy: ASUS's volume 15.6" budget chassis dressed with the newest low-cost Intel refresh silicon and padded RAM. The design bets that buyers shop CPU/RAM numbers first: a real 6-core with 16GB upgradable DDR5 at an aggressive sale price, paid for with a dim 250-nit panel, a flexy all-plastic chassis, and a stripped USB-C (data only). The 16GB tier is the config to own — the twin 8GB SKU gives up little savings logic.
